title: Transformation Stage Domain
outOfScope: Evidence acquisition, source adapters, persistence, scheduling, ranking, reporting, Telegram delivery, scoring, and stage recommendation
Automatic stage inference, proof quality calculation, external identity resolution, or runtime enforcement of transition policy
Cross-feature imports and new Cargo dependencies

sources.reason: Repository operating rules and validation requirements.
Canonical Work Item and governance terminology.
Layer direction and Domain isolation rules.
Six stages, transition discipline, persistence, and explicit proof categories.
Evidence polarity, confidence, freshness, and explicit missing requirements.
Stage upgrade boundaries and persistence requirements.
Stage is not replaced by a score.
Predecessor evidence boundary and current-WI execution convention.

riskAssessment.reason: Transformation stage is a high-leverage research conclusion. The Domain must retain explicit transitions and proof polarity without automatically inferring or recommending a stage.
riskAssessment.reviewNotes: Evidence quality, source acquisition, persistence calculation, ranking, and stage recommendation remain deferred.

reasons: Transformation stage code and tests require the standard governed review route.

executionDecision.reason: The explicit user authorization covers execution and Contract recording for all 24 roadmap Work Items.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: src/features/transformation/domain exposes the six Stage variants TOOL, SUBSTITUTION, WORKFLOW, PRODUCTION_SYSTEM, PRODUCTIVITY_BREAKOUT, and REFERENCE_MODEL with stable ordering metadata.
StageTransition preserves explicit from/to stages, rejects same-stage transitions, allows both upgrades and corrections/downgrades, and retains transition date facts.
TransformationProofSet preserves supporting, counter, and missing proof collections in insertion order with deterministic duplicate rejection.
PersistenceFact preserves the supplied persistence window and observation count without calculating persistence or promoting a stage.
The Domain remains independent of infrastructure, interface, network, database, LLM, external source, and other feature modules.
Focused unit and integration tests cover six stages, transition boundaries, proof polarity, missing proof, persistence facts, duplicate rejection, and downgrade support.
The design spec and execution plan record the transformation boundary, no-goals, authorization, current-WI issue rule, and verification commands.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Keep Transformation Domain independent of external systems and other feature modules.
Keep Stage distinct from Score; preserve explicit transition direction and evidence proof polarity.
Represent missing proof explicitly; do not turn absence into support or a stage conclusion.
Do not add dependencies for this contract.
Resolve issues within the current Work Item when they remain inside its Contract scope; open a successor only for a distinct or materially expanded boundary.
Do not introduce trading, price prediction, or capital-action behavior.

intent.problem: The repository lacks a typed model for six transformation stages, explicit stage transitions, supporting/counter/missing proof, and persistence facts.
constraints: Retain supplied stage, transition, proof, missing-requirement, persistence-window, and observation-count facts. Perform no stage recommendation.
Preserve transition direction, counter evidence, missing proof, and downgrade support as explicit facts. Perform no automatic inference.
Transformation Domain stays provider-agnostic. Use existing Rust conventions. No cross-feature imports.
intent.rationale: A pure transformation model gives later Stage Gate, Ranking, and Reporting WIs an auditable state structure while keeping evidence interpretation outside the Domain.
